description: Reference for the CI retrieval-benchmark gate (run_retrieval_benchmark --gate-against). Regenerate whenever the pinned commits in .github/actions/benchmark-index/action.yml, the questions, or retrieval behaviour intentionally change.
how_to_regenerate: Build the index as in .github/actions/benchmark-index/action.yml (GRAPHDB_ENABLED=False), run `python manage.py run_retrieval_benchmark --quiet --output report.json` from a checkout WITHOUT backend/.env (CI has none, and a developer .env can set other values and shifts results; the code default of RETRIEVAL_MAX_SAME_SOURCE_PATH is 1, as on dev and prod), then copy the baseline/graph hit_at_* and mrr_at_* values from report.json['aggregate'].
what_this_baseline_is: This is a guard against regressions in the retrieval code, nothing more. It is an index of the old cut with deterministic hash vectors, GraphDB off. It does not measure the prepared cut that production serves (prepared index, 384-number half-precision vector index, 100 probes), because CI has no semantic embedder. The one CI measurement of the prepared cut with hash vectors is in docs/plans/2026-11-15-sources-prepared-for-semantic-search.md, section 10, step 5: hit@10 0.383, a drop I take to be an effect of hash vectors on the smaller pieces, not a fault of the cut. Do not read these numbers as production quality.

environment.generated_with: CI runs 44498711080 (PR #555) and 44498766640 (workflow_dispatch on the same branch): identical aggregates to four decimals, with the per-file limit at its new default of 1
environment.index: old cut (INDEX_CUT_VERSION=0), built with build_source_index, no prepare_index

previous.generated_with: CI run 40497844709 (PR #162): its benchmark-report.json aggregate, after the OpRa questions were changed to expect the files that define each concept
previous.reason: RETRIEVAL_MAX_SAME_SOURCE_PATH defaulted to 2 then; the default is now 1 (as on dev and prod). The run of 2026-11-18 (CI run 44204496420, the old cut, limit 2) gave hit@10 0.483 / 0.497 and MRR@10 0.266 / 0.281 (baseline / graph), so the file's figures held; the shift to 0.517 comes with the limit.
